headline: Agentic AI Goes Mainstream: From LLM Selection Systems to Production Agents Cutting Real Work
summary: A cluster of InfoQ pieces this week trace how agentic AI is moving from concept to production. A presentation details architecture patterns for building LLM-powered selection systems that narrow thousands of options down to one. SpaceXAI launched 'Grok Bot' for autonomous AI agents, Grab reported cutting mechanical analytics work from 44% to 30% using AI agents, an article explores 'agentic fitness functions' as an extension of evolutionary architecture beyond deterministic rules, and a podcast with Tracy Bannon debates whether agentic AI risks becoming a 'Sorcerer's Apprentice' scenario - powerful but hard to control.
why_it_matters: This is directly relevant to your work building LLM applications on ServiceNow and your goal of becoming an AI Application Engineer. The LLM selection systems presentation and agentic fitness functions article offer concrete architecture patterns you could apply to your own agent designs, while Grab's real-world metrics (44%→30% analytics workload) give you a benchmark for pitching agentic automation ROI internally. Bannon's podcast is a useful counterpoint on governance and control risks worth considering as you design autonomous agents.

headline: Australia's Skilled Migration Overhaul Deepens Political Rift Ahead of 2026-27
summary: Absolute Immigration outlines 2026-27 state-by-state skilled migration updates across Australia, signaling changes to nomination pathways and occupation lists. Separately, the Coalition has revealed a surprise new immigration target, but this has exposed a widening internal 'wedge' within the party over migration policy, as reported by news24.com.au and The Australian, with disagreement over how aggressively to cut intake numbers.
why_it_matters: As a skilled migrant-adjacent professional based in Adelaide, changes to state nomination programs and occupation lists could directly affect visa pathways relevant to tech/engineering roles. The political disagreement within the Coalition also signals potential volatility in future migration policy, which is worth monitoring if you're tracking pathways to permanent residency or advising others in similar situations.
